title: Initial navigation performance before and after optimization

premeasurementRevisions.scope: Deployment identity readback transport provenance only; timing settings, cache policy, metrics, sample count and budgets are unchanged.
premeasurementRevisions.reason: The Node public health readback failed before any performance trial. A normal anonymous public browser navigation was observed to return the expected identity. Use the same public endpoint through a separate pinned Chrome navigation and fail closed if it is denied.

premeasurementRevisions.scope: Browser-process launch policy on the disposable GitHub-hosted measurement runner only; timing settings, cache policy, metrics, sample count and budgets are unchanged.
premeasurementRevisions.reason: The diagnostic run confirmed that the browser could not launch with its default sandbox on this runner. Use the same process-local --no-sandbox policy as the repository's successful pinned Playwright browser probe, only for disposable GitHub-hosted audit processes. Public navigation denials still fail closed.

browserLaunch.activation: Only when GITHUB_ACTIONS=true and RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT=github-hosted. A different local environment retains its default sandbox and is outside this fixed CI comparison.
browserLaunch.observation: Record noSandboxObserved from the actual launched process spawnargs membership; retain only the bounded explicit flags, never raw argv.
browserLaunch.credentialScope: No application secrets, authenticated browser state or credentials are supplied to these fresh browser processes; their environment uses the existing bounded allowlist.
browserLaunch.unchangedControls: No app, OS, firewall, account authorization, proxy or request-fingerprint workaround is introduced. This isolated browser-process security policy is distinct from website access controls.

deploymentReadback.profile: A separate fresh anonymous Chrome process and temporary profile; never reuse the measured browser or its resource cache.
deploymentReadback.timing: Outside the Lighthouse trace and timed measurement. A pretrial readback browser closes before the measured browser starts; a post-trace readback starts only after the timed trace has ended.
deploymentReadback.requestPolicy: Ordinary public GET navigation with the browser's default request behavior; no credentials, custom user agent or headers, proxy, reused authenticated session, or app/host/account access-control changes. The process-local sandbox policy is explicitly declared in browserLaunch.
deploymentReadback.failurePolicy: Denied navigation, unexpected final URL, unsuccessful response or source/deployment identity mismatch remains a failed readback; no access-control changes or forced continuation.

scope.claim: same-session unpaired lab change at the canonical production hostname
limitations: All before samples precede deployment; all after samples follow deployment. This is not an alternating or paired experiment.
Deployment time, CDN state, backend load, public content, network conditions and third-party responses can confound the observed change.
Five valid observations per viewport and phase support this task-local diagnostic, not the repository's global field or G003 admission requirements.
CPU slowdown is relative to the runner. Viewport and request-level throttling do not reproduce a physical mobile or tablet device.
Both phases use the existing __qa=render-flow query to exclude synthetic traffic from field telemetry. Sanitized report URLs omit the query; this exclusion is not an ordinary-user RUM observation.
The canonical hostname remains constant so origin-bound map integrations are exercised under the same URL.

sampling.runnerContinuity: Same GitHub Actions job, runner and attempt for both phases; deployment occurs during a bounded wait between phases.
sampling.invalidTrials: retain all failed attempts; never replace their status with pass
sampling.extraRuns: Only to resolve a documented concrete invalidity or instability; preserve the original attempts and the reason.

tti.targetBasis: task-specific engineering target, not current Core Web Vitals

controlsReady.targetBasis: task-specific engineering target, not TTI or Core Web Vitals

mapReady.targetBasis: task-specific engineering target, not TTI or Core Web Vitals

controlsReady.desktop: First observed homeChromeReady=true AND a visible button[data-desktop-map-menu-trigger][aria-haspopup=menu][aria-expanded] AND a visible input[name=desktop-left-panel-restaurant-search]; wrapper readiness alone does not qualify.

applicationTimings.mapReady: First observation of a visible loaded Naver map tile from pstatic.net/naver.com/naver.net/ntruss.com (at least 100 CSS px in each dimension, complete and naturalWidth > 0) AND a visible cluster or restaurant marker element.
applicationTimings.desktopPanelValidity: homePanelReady=true AND a visible desktop panel AND zero visible panel alerts AND at least one popular restaurant item AND at least one latest restaurant item.
applicationTimings.capture: Read-only DOM observation installed before application scripts, sampled every 100 milliseconds. Preserve the qualifying state and first observed timestamp.
applicationTimings.throttlingBoundary: Count an application timing only when it is no later than the Lighthouse observedTraceEnd. Later observations occur after Lighthouse may reset throttling and remain contextual observations only.
applicationTimings.missing: Retain null when not observed; never use the observation timeout or TTI as an invented value.
applicationTimings.interpretation: These application-specific timings reveal when usable controls and the populated map appear even if a skeleton is an early LCP candidate. They do not replace TTI.

comparison.improvedWhen: beforeMedian - afterMedian >= minimumReduction AND relativeReduction >= 0.10 AND beforeMedian - afterMedian > noise
comparison.regressedWhen: afterMedian - beforeMedian >= minimumReduction AND relativeIncrease >= 0.10 AND afterMedian - beforeMedian > noise

evidence.rawReports: Retained sanitized Lighthouse report, trace, network summary, observations and screenshot for every attempted trial.
evidence.sourceBinding: Each phase supplies a frozen source SHA, tree SHA and deployment identity, corroborated by the browser observation.
evidence.integrity: SHA-256 artifact map with a detached expected hash supplied to scorer and validator.
evidence.validator: Independently rederive metric values, medians, MADs, gates and sample eligibility from mapped raw inputs; do not import scorer logic.
